policy.roster: Complete exact 2024–25 CCD LEA 5101260 / VA-029 directory, including all statuses, complete retained total/grade membership and lunch rows. Missing native school profiles remain explicit holds; names never join.
policy.identity: CCD ST_SCHID is VA-029- plus the already complete seven-digit native division/school key. Remove only that exact prefix and cross-check division 29 and the native school number from the same official profile. Never prepend division again, match names, or infer missing profiles.
policy.native_populations: Reuse the audited Virginia 2024–25 enrolled-grade contract: positive grades 3–8 only, high-only, and mixed grade 3–8 plus grades 9–12 are separate prospective populations. Positive unrecognized grades remain unclassified. Offered-versus-enrolled and strict CCD offered intersections are completeness diagnostics, never new population filters.
policy.income: Same-year September 30 school Fall Membership, individually classified economically disadvantaged if eligible for free/reduced-price meals, receiving TANF, eligible for Medicaid, or migrant or experiencing homelessness. This broader student economic-status measure is distinct from the portal meal-service measure, which counts every student in CEP divisions.
policy.income_reconciliation: Use native same-profile All Students and ED counts only when ED and non-ED exactly sum to All Students and every year-matched grade subtotal and total reconcile. Every required count and published ED percentage must be unsuppressed. Retain stale display percentages; never infer suppressed counts or replace missing native status with CCD direct certification.
policy.assessment: Native School Quality profile subject option 0, All Students subgroup 5, 2024-2025 Mathematics or English Reading Passed table/chart values. SOL plus VAAP; proficient plus advanced. Direct whole-subject totals only; no grade/course averaging. Retain every displayed year and raw performance category, but spring 2025 new 2023 mathematics and 2024 English standards exclude older years from the proposed snapshot.
policy.types: Retain all authoritative CCD charter/type flags and current native category labels. Current labels, names, offered grades, selective admissions and fit quality never filter the native source populations. This extract does not establish admissions classifications or virtual status.
policy.counts: No verified exact valid-score denominator. Enrollment, ED counts, CCD membership, portal Record Count, and participation never substitute for tested counts. Every verified denominator, sampling variance and interval stays unavailable for every prospective model.
policy.combined: Equal mean of eligible Math and ELA native pass percentages, not the fraction proficient in both.
policy.approval: Source/cohort audit only: status and scope audit_pending; source/modeling approvals false. Prospective grade-school release requires independent numerical diagnostics, canonical integration and browser checks. High/mixed cohorts below 30 remain unreleased; no fits are produced.

planning.explanation: Discovery only. Exact IDs and original membership must reconcile independently; planning does not approve native outcomes, income, population membership or high/mixed models.

raw: Data Notes for the Common Core of Data (CCD) Universe Files

This file includes background information on the data file release separated into state data notes, metadata provided by states, and post-submission data revisions. The information is provided in separate tabs and described below:

Data Notes (green tab) - this table provides information on data anomalies in the CCD data files. The filters on the column headers can be used to filter the notes to a data file or issue type. Note that the notes tie the comments states provided to specific data errors. Refer to the CCD Business Rules tab for more information on each error. Also note that the error row includes the NCES LEA or school ID for all entities flagged with that error (as appropriate).
CCD Grades Offered Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state on the grades offered within the state beyond the standard grades PK-12 (ungraded, G13, adult education).

CCD Membership Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state the state can differentiate grades offered versus grades enrolled at the district level as well as several fields that provide more information related to prekindergarten and kindergarten enrollment.
CCD Staff FTE Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state teachers may be assigned to ungraded classes.

CCD Business Rules (yellow tab) - This tab shows the rule logic for all errors references in the State Notes tab. The CCD Business Rules are part of the much broader master EDFacts Business Rules Single Inventory (BRSI). Please refer to the BRSI User Guide for the detailed description of each column. The master EDFacts BRSI provides information on historical changes in busness rules from prior years.
Post-submission data revisions (purple tab) - This tab lists all of the post-submission data revisions/adjustments that were made in the SEA statistical file prior to file release.
Abbreviation Index (orange tab) - This tab provides a description of acronyms used within this document.
Note:  Throughout this document, references to states may include both states and jurisdictions.

The laws governing the California Longitudinal Pupil Data Achievement System (CALPADS) are limited to K-12 students and schools. California preschools are governed differently than K-12 schools and do not fit the model of the California Department of Education’s (CDE) longitudinal data system. While the CDE does collect some data about preschool students, including students receiving special education and related services as required by law, not all preschool programs in the state are statutorily required to report data to the CDE or CALPADS. Only programs with a CDS code and students with a unique student identifier can be reported to CALPADS. This results in an incomplete preschool data set that isn’t representative of the educational landscape in California. Reporting incomplete data sets for public consumption could result in misrepresentation of student groups and diminished reliability of publicly available data provided by the CDE.

The California Department of Education (CDE) Nutrition Services Division collects data on all nutrition programs in the state using unique numerical entity identifiers assigned by the Child Nutrition Information and Payment System (CNIPS). Because not all nutrition programs in California are associated with schools or districts, they are not issued the CDE’s statewide unique identifier known as the "CDS code". In previous years, only a limited number of nutrition programs could be linked to their corresponding CDS codes. This reporting year, however, the CDE has successfully linked a greater number of schools to their CNIPS IDs. The CDE continues to work on migrating CNIPS to our internal servers to improve reporting capabilities—particularly for NSLP Provision status—for all reportable entities in future years.

Data are accurate. There are several reasons why this may happen. Direct Certification matches children from a list from ODHS to where the student is listed as enrolling according to the most recent ADM report. The F&R data comes from October meal claims as entered by school districts. If the enrollment boundaries change between the school year, students may have shifted from one school to the next. Districts may have entered meal claim data incorrectly. We do not currently have any system to check these values against when approving claims. Finally, some schools may enter data only for students who ate meals during that month. If a school has a large number of students who are directly certified but choose to not eat meals provided by the school, this contributes to this value as well.

Race data, especially for minority races, can vary from year to year since there is no mandate for reporting the same race every year. The data has been analyzed over the years and LEA reporting of this data for individual students is inconsistent. For example, one year a particular student might be reported as American Indian/Alaskan Native but the following year reported in more than one race (multiracial) category or vice versa. SY2425 race data was compared to SY2324 data for some minority races & this was found to hold true for data reported for SY2425 as well. Also, Vermont’s student population was around 87% white in SY2425 and with minority race populations being small and disaggregated by race and sex, small changes from year to year can result in a change in count of more than 10 and percentage changes greater than 10 percent, the thresholds for this check.

The LEA/SEA AE student counts dropped significantly in SY25 due in large part to fewer students being reported by SU099 Department of Corrections. According to DOC staff, re-organization of the Program Services Division (now known as Risk Intervention Services Division [RIS]) within the Department of Corrections and the subsequent re-alignment of their Student Information Services allowed them to subdivide students into multiple “schools”  for Behavioral Health/Clinical services, Vocational services, Foundational Education, and Community High School of Vermont (CHSVT, an independent school run by DOC) and either aggregate the data or extract distinct data sets for each service. Beginning with SY 2024-2025, they only included individuals actively enrolled in the CHSVT school as of October 1. In the past, they had included all active enrollees without HS diplomas taking Education Foundations remedial reading, writing and mathematics courses as well, but in an October 2025 meeting with VT AOE, all participants concurred that they would only include individuals currently taking high school level academic courses (and exclude those taking vocational training and behavioral health courses).
 
In addition, the number of AE students reported at public schools dropped significantly from 45 in SY24 to 11 in SY25, continuing a declining trend at Vermont public school for at least the past five years. Nine schools that reported AE students in both SY23 & SY24 reported none in SY25. Essex High School (PS388), the school with the most AE students in SY23 & SY24, 17 in SY23 students and 18 in SY24, reported 0 in SY25.

West Virginia has a relatively homogeneous population. As a result, even minor variations that naturally occur within cohort populations may appear as significant differences when disaggregated by individual subgroups.

In recent years, the state has seen an increase in the number of educational programs and circumstances—such as the HOPE Scholarship and homeschooling—that require children not enrolled in public PK–12 schools to obtain a student identification number from the state’s student information system (WVEIS). According to state law, these children are not required to provide any student attribute information (including race/ethnicity) when obtaining an ID number. However, if they later enroll in a public PK–12 school, either full- or part-time, the collection of student attribute data is expected to be completed at the time of enrollment.

Additionally, as users become more proficient with the new student information system, improvements in data accuracy and subgroup classification are ongoing. This increased precision may result in some students—previously categorized in one subgroup—being more accurately reclassified into a different subgroup or multiple subgroups.

fragments.label: assessment_scope
fragments.raw_markup: The annual pass rate data reported on the Assessment tab includes all grade level and content area state assessments (Standards of Learning assessments and Virginia Alternate Assessment Program assessments).

fragments.label: reading_population
fragments.raw_markup: This chart displays the percentage of students passing state reading tests. Virginia students are assessed annually in reading in grades 3-8 and once in high school with an end-of-course (EOC) reading test. Use the drop down menu above the chart to view results for a specific test. Use the menu below the chart to select results for a specific group of students. Practice test items representative of the content and skills included in current Standards of Learning assessments are available on the Virginia Department of Education website to assist in understanding the format of the tests and questions.

fragments.label: math_population
fragments.raw_markup: This chart displays the percentage of students passing state mathematics tests. Virginia students are assessed annually in mathematics in grades 3-8 and at the end of secondary courses (Algebra I, Geometry and Algebra II) as needed to meet graduation requirements. Use the drop down menu above the chart to view results for a specific test. Use the menu below the chart to select results for a specific group of students. Practice test items representative of the content and skills included in current Standards of Learning assessments are available on the Virginia Department of Education website to assist in understanding the format of the tests and questions.

raw: Data Notes for the Common Core of Data (CCD) Universe Files

This file includes background information on the data file release separated into state data notes, metadata provided by states, and post-submission data revisions. The information is provided in separate tabs and described below:

Data Notes (green tab) - this table provides information on data anomalies in the CCD data files. The filters on the column headers can be used to filter the notes to a data file or issue type. Note that the notes tie the comments states provided to specific data errors. Refer to the CCD Business Rules tab for more information on each error. Also note that the error row includes the NCES LEA or school ID for all entities flagged with that error (as appropriate).
CCD Grades Offered Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state on the grades offered within the state beyond the standard grades PK-12 (ungraded, G13, adult education).

CCD Membership Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state the state can differentiate grades offered versus grades enrolled at the district level as well as several fields that provide more information related to prekindergarten and kindergarten enrollment.
CCD Staff FTE Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state teachers may be assigned to ungraded classes.

CCD Business Rules (yellow tab) - This tab shows the rule logic for all errors references in the State Notes tab. The CCD Business Rules are part of the much broader master EDFacts Business Rules Single Inventory (BRSI). Please refer to the BRSI User Guide for the detailed description of each column. The master EDFacts BRSI provides information on historical changes in busness rules from prior years.
Post-submission data revisions (purple tab) - This tab lists all of the post-submission data revisions/adjustments that were made in the SEA statistical file prior to file release.
Abbreviation Index (orange tab) - This tab provides a description of acronyms used within this document.
Note:  Throughout this document, references to states may include both states and jurisdictions.
The total Direct Certification was greater than the count of students reported as Free Lunch Qualified.
Data shown was submitted by the LEAs and is considered valid as reported. This error is due to the fact that our Direct Certification EUT includes students certified for both free and reduced lunch.
Directory, CCD School, Free and Reduced Price Lunch, Membership
Direct Certification or Free and Reduced-Price Lunch was not reported for a school with membership that has the National School Lunch Program.
All of the schools listed are PK-only schools.  As such, we do not include their F/R lunch numbers in the data we report.
Directory, Free and Reduced Price Lunch
Free and Reduced Price Lunch was reported for a reportable program.

Forrest Hills Community Development Center is a site under Fairfield City BOE.  This site houses multiple different school types under one roof, but there is at least one Pre-K class that has Fairfield City board enrolled Pre-K children that should be counted towards CEP numbers.  This is why we have it listed as a CEP site within our CNP Online Application.
The count of students reported for Free and Reduced-Price Lunch in the SEA in the current SY varied significantly from the prior SY.

The data owners have verified that this rule failure is due to the roll back on households eligible for Medicaid.  Beginning April 1, 2025 when we captured our data used to qualify schools for CEP, we noticed a ~6% decrease in directly certified students across the state.
Membership was not reported for an operational LEA.
These schools are not under the State Board of Education and therefore their data is not part of our reporting. They are State operated schools funded directly by the Legislature outside of K12.
Staff FTE was not reported or was reported as zero for an operational LEA. Report -1 if the staff counts are not available.
These schools are not under the State Board of Education and therefore their data is not part of our reporting. They are State operated schools funded directly by the Legislature outside of K12.
The FTE in the SEA reported by Staff Category (CCD) in the current SY varied significantly from the prior SY.

This data is accurate as reported.  The logic in the stored procedure pulls from the financial data and sums the FTE by SSN where the person has a teacher object code, and it matches it to fall schedule data and takes the max grade for that teacher.  Additionally, if the grade shows up as NULL in the schedule data, it sets it to PK.
The count of schools by NSLP Status in the SEA in the current SY varied significantly from the prior SY.

The laws governing the California Longitudinal Pupil Data Achievement System (CALPADS) are limited to K-12 students and schools. California preschools are governed differently than K-12 schools and do not fit the model of the California Department of Education’s (CDE) longitudinal data system. While the CDE does collect some data about preschool students, including students receiving special education and related services as required by law, not all preschool programs in the state are statutorily required to report data to the CDE or CALPADS. Only programs with a CDS code and students with a unique student identifier can be reported to CALPADS. This results in an incomplete preschool data set that isn’t representative of the educational landscape in California. Reporting incomplete data sets for public consumption could result in misrepresentation of student groups and diminished reliability of publicly available data provided by the CDE.

The California Department of Education (CDE) Nutrition Services Division collects data on all nutrition programs in the state using unique numerical entity identifiers assigned by the Child Nutrition Information and Payment System (CNIPS). Because not all nutrition programs in California are associated with schools or districts, they are not issued the CDE’s statewide unique identifier known as the "CDS code". In previous years, only a limited number of nutrition programs could be linked to their corresponding CDS codes. This reporting year, however, the CDE has successfully linked a greater number of schools to their CNIPS IDs. The CDE continues to work on migrating CNIPS to our internal servers to improve reporting capabilities—particularly for NSLP Provision status—for all reportable entities in future years.

The total Direct Certification was greater than the count of students reported as Free Lunch Qualified.

Data are accurate. There are several reasons why this may happen. Direct Certification matches children from a list from ODHS to where the student is listed as enrolling according to the most recent ADM report. The F&R data comes from October meal claims as entered by school districts. If the enrollment boundaries change between the school year, students may have shifted from one school to the next. Districts may have entered meal claim data incorrectly. We do not currently have any system to check these values against when approving claims. Finally, some schools may enter data only for students who ate meals during that month. If a school has a large number of students who are directly certified but choose to not eat meals provided by the school, this contributes to this value as well.

For example, one year a particular student might be reported as American Indian/Alaskan Native but the following year reported in more than one race (multiracial) category or vice versa. SY2425 race data was compared to SY2324 data for some minority races & this was found to hold true for data reported for SY2425 as well. Also, Vermont’s student population was around 87% white in SY2425 and with minority race populations being small and disaggregated by race and sex, small changes from year to year can result in a change in count of more than 10 and percentage changes greater than 10 percent, the thresholds for this check.

West Virginia has a relatively homogeneous population. As a result, even minor variations that naturally occur within cohort populations may appear as significant differences when disaggregated by individual subgroups.

In recent years, the state has seen an increase in the number of educational programs and circumstances—such as the HOPE Scholarship and homeschooling—that require children not enrolled in public PK–12 schools to obtain a student identification number from the state’s student information system (WVEIS). According to state law, these children are not required to provide any student attribute information (including race/ethnicity) when obtaining an ID number. However, if they later enroll in a public PK–12 school, either full- or part-time, the collection of student attribute data is expected to be completed at the time of enrollment.

Additionally, as users become more proficient with the new student information system, improvements in data accuracy and subgroup classification are ongoing. This increased precision may result in some students—previously categorized in one subgroup—being more accurately reclassified into a different subgroup or multiple subgroups.

While the CDE does collect some data about preschool students, including students receiving special education and related services as required by law, not all preschool programs in the state are statutorily required to report data to the CDE or CALPADS. fragments.raw_markup: The annual pass rate data reported on the Assessment tab includes all grade level and content area state assessments (Standards of Learning assessments and Virginia Alternate Assessment Program assessments).

fragments.label: reading_population
fragments.raw_markup: This chart displays the percentage of students passing state reading tests. Virginia students are assessed annually in reading in grades 3-8 and once in high school with an end-of-course (EOC) reading test. Use the drop down menu above the chart to view results for a specific test. Use the menu below the chart to select results for a specific group of students. Practice test items representative of the content and skills included in current Standards of Learning assessments are available on the Virginia Department of Education website to assist in understanding the format of the tests and questions.

fragments.label: math_population
fragments.raw_markup: This chart displays the percentage of students passing state mathematics tests. Use the drop down menu above the chart to view results for a specific test. Use the menu below the chart to select results for a specific group of students. Practice test items representative of the content and skills included in current Standards of Learning assessments are available on the Virginia Department of Education website to assist in understanding the format of the tests and questions.

fragments.label: individual_economic_status
fragments.raw_markup:
A student is reported as economically disadvantaged if he or she meets any one of the following criteria:
  • Is eligible for Free/Reduced Meals;
  • Receives Temporary Assistance for Needy Families;
  • Is eligible for Medicaid; or
  • Is a migrant or is experiencing homelessness.

fragments.label: assessment_scope
fragments.raw_markup: The annual pass rate data reported on the Assessment tab includes all grade level and content area state assessments (Standards of Learning assessments and Virginia Alternate Assessment Program assessments).

fragments.label: reading_population
fragments.raw_markup: This chart displays the percentage of students passing state reading tests. Virginia students are assessed annually in reading in grades 3-8 and once in high school with an end-of-course (EOC) reading test. Use the drop down menu above the chart to view results for a specific test. Use the menu below the chart to select results for a specific group of students. Practice test items representative of the content and skills included in current Standards of Learning assessments are available on the Virginia Department of Education website to assist in understanding the format of the tests and questions.

fragments.label: math_population
fragments.raw_markup: This chart displays the percentage of students passing state mathematics tests. Virginia students are assessed annually in mathematics in grades 3-8 and at the end of secondary courses (Algebra I, Geometry and Algebra II) as needed to meet graduation requirements. Use the drop down menu above the chart to view results for a specific test. Use the menu below the chart to select results for a specific group of students. Practice test items representative of the content and skills included in current Standards of Learning assessments are available on the Virginia Department of Education website to assist in understanding the format of the tests and questions.

Complete CCD notes are supplemental, never substituted for native ED.

high: Only 23 usable schools per subject; below prospective 30-school floor.
mixed: Only one usable school per subject; below prospective 30-school floor.
unclassified: Three native primary-only profiles and Lake Braddock with positive Post Graduate enrollment have no classified native assessment population.
missing_native: 28 exact operational CCD schools lack audited native profiles; no native income or outcomes are substituted.

coverage_notes: Grade-school source membership is complete for 162 exact operational native profiles: 152 usable per subject and ten native income exclusions. Numerical, canonical and browser release gates remain pending.
24 exact directory programs report NOGRADES=Yes, every offered-grade flag No, and no original CCD membership rows. Absence is not zero or Ungraded enrollment.
Four missing-native preschool centers have 784 reported CCD pupils. CCD membership/lunch never supply missing native status or rates.
Fifteen native profiles across all bands have unavailable or unreconciled individual economic status; no masked grade, ED or non-ED count is inferred.
